name: Mahaha
description: The Mahaha is a malevolent spirit of Inuit oral tradition: a thin, blue-skinned, perpetually grinning demon of the Arctic that ambushes lone travellers and tickles them to death with long, sharp-clawed fingers, leaving its victims with a frozen smile.
full_description: The Mahaha is a malevolent spirit in Inuit oral tradition, associated particularly with the icy expanses of the Canadian Arctic. Stories describe it as a gaunt, blue-skinned, semi-skeletal humanoid with stringy black hair, white pupil-less eyes, a permanent maniacal grin, and long, bony fingers tipped with sharp icy claws. The Mahaha hunts lone travellers in remote and exposed parts of the tundra and ice; rather than killing with violence it tickles its victims to death, the combination of involuntary laughter, exposure, and terror leaving them dead with a frozen grin matching its own. According to Inuit oral tradition, the Mahaha can be defeated by tricking it into bending over a stream or fishing hole; the victim then pushes it into the water, after which the spirit cannot return. The Mahaha functions in Inuit storytelling as a cautionary figure warning against straying alone from camp and emphasising community and shared survival in an unforgiving environment. The figure is documented in 20th-century compilations of Inuit oral traditions and in popular cryptid- and folklore-aimed sources; it does not appear to be tied to a single historical incident and is not part of the cryptozoological literature.
origin: Mahaha stories are part of Inuit oral tradition across the Canadian Arctic (Inuit Nunangat); they are best documented in popular folklore writing rather than in tightly-localised regional accounts.

etymology.origin: Inuktitut name preserved in Inuit oral tradition; not analysed in the secondary sources consulted.
etymology.meaning: Not glossed in the available sources.
etymology.first_use: Documented in 20th-century English-language compilations of Inuit oral tradition; the underlying tradition is older.

timeline.event: Inuit oral traditions of the Mahaha are recorded by 20th-century ethnographers and storytellers
timeline.significance: Cultural baseline of the documented figure
timeline.source: Inuit oral tradition (compiled at inuitmyths.com and Mythlok)

cultural_notes: The Mahaha story encodes a community ethic — stay with your people, share warmth, do not boast or wander — through fear of a memorable Arctic spirit.
